blocks.title: 1. The Core Concept: The Number Ninja
blocks.content: In advanced exams, factoring quadratics isn't the main question; it's just step 1 of a massive 5-step calculus problem. You cannot afford to spend 3 minutes thinking about what numbers multiply to 24 and add to 10. The **Polynomials Gym** forces your brain to memorize these common number pairs so you can factorise instantly.

blocks.title: 2. The Strategy: Sign Recognition
blocks.content:
Before you even think about the numbers, look at the SIGNS (+ and -). They tell you everything you need to know about the brackets!

� If the last number is POSITIVE (e.g., x� + 5x **+ 6**), the two brackets MUST have the exact SAME sign. (Look at the middle term to see if they are both + or both -).
� If the last number is NEGATIVE (e.g., x� + x **- 12**), the two brackets MUST have DIFFERENT signs (one +, one -). No exceptions!

blocks.title: 3. Step-by-Step: The Mental Scan
blocks.content:
1. Scan the last sign: is it + or -?
2. Mentally load up the bracket templates: (x + )(x + ) or (x + )(x - ).
3. Look at the last number and rapidly cycle its factors in your head (24 is 12&2, 8&3, 6&4).
4. Pick the pair that hits the middle target number.
5. Slap them into the brackets.

blocks.title: 4. Worked Example: High Speed Factoring
blocks.content:
Mentally factorise **x� - 8x + 15** in 3 seconds.

� **Mental Step 1 (Signs):** Last sign is +, so they match. Middle sign is -, so they are BOTH negative. Template: (x - )(x - ).
� **Mental Step 2 (Factors):** Factors of 15 are 1&15 or 3&5.
� **Mental Step 3 (Target):** We need to make -8. -3 and -5 makes -8!
� **Mental Step 4 (Execute):** Write down (x - 3)(x - 5).

blocks.title: 5. Common Pitfalls
blocks.content: The trap of the number 12! When students see **x� - x - 12**, they panic and pick 6 & 2. (6 - 2 = 4, not 1!). Then they try 12 & 1. They forget about 4 & 3! When dealing with numbers like 12, 24, and 36, students often forget the factors sitting right in the middle of the times tables. Always check the 'middle' factors first!
